import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
fig.suptitle('Dog Registration Analysis in Zurich, Switzerland', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

# Plot 1: Top 10 Dog Breeds
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
top_breeds = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().head(10)
colors1 = sns.color_palette('viridis', 10)
bars1 = ax1.barh(top_breeds.index[::-1], top_breeds.values[::-1], color=colors1)
ax1.set_xlabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Breed', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_title('Top 10 Most Popular Dog Breeds', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.bar_label(bars1, padding=3, fontsize=9)

# Plot 2: Distribution by District (Kreis)
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
district_counts = df.groupby('KreisLang')['AnzHunde'].sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
colors2 = sns.color_palette('coolwarm', len(district_counts))
bars2 = ax2.bar(range(len(district_counts)), district_counts.values, color=colors2)
ax2.set_xticks(range(len(district_counts)))
ax2.set_xticklabels([k.replace('Kreis ', '') for k in district_counts.index], rotation=45, ha='right')
ax2.set_xlabel('District', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title('Dog Distribution by District', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Plot 3: Dog Age Distribution
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
age_counts = df.groupby(['AlterVHundLang', 'AlterVHundSort'])['AnzHunde'].sum().reset_index()
age_counts = age_counts.sort_values('AlterVHundSort')
# Filter out very old ages with few dogs for cleaner visualization
age_counts = age_counts[age_counts['AlterVHundSort'] <= 15]
colors3 = sns.color_palette('mako', len(age_counts))
ax3.bar(age_counts['AlterVHundLang'], age_counts['AnzHunde'], color=colors3)
ax3.set_xlabel('Dog Age', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_title('Distribution of Dog Ages', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# Plot 4: Dog Gender Distribution with Owner Gender
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
gender_crosstab = pd.crosstab(df['SexLang'], df['SexHundLang'], values=df['AnzHunde'], aggfunc='sum')
gender_crosstab.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax4, color=['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4', '#95E1D3'], edgecolor='black', width=0.7)
ax4.set_xlabel('Owner Gender', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_ylabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_title('Dog Gender by Owner Gender', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.legend(title='Dog Gender', loc='upper right')
ax4.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=0)

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
